The must-sees

12 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Bridge · 1402

    Charles Bridge

    Charles IV laid the foundation stone in 1357 and Peter Parler’s workshop built it. Most statues on the parapets today are copies; many originals are kept in the Lapidarium and at Vyšehrad.

    Look for

    Under the St John of Nepomuk statue, two bronze reliefs are rubbed shiny by hands. A small cross on the parapet marks where he is said to have been thrown.

  2. 02
    Church

    Church of Our Lady before Týn

    For two centuries it was the main church of the Hussite reform movement in the Old Town. The Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe, who worked for Emperor Rudolf II, is buried inside.

    Look for

    Tycho Brahe’s red marble tombstone is on a pillar near the altar, showing him in armour.

  3. 03
    Building · 1996

    Dancing House

    Vlado Milunić and Frank Gehry designed it on a corner left empty by an American air raid in February 1945. Václav Havel, who lived next door, supported the project.

    Look for

    On top of the building sits a twisted metal dome nicknamed the Medusa.

  4. 04
    Neighbourhood

    Josefov (Jewish Quarter)

    It is named after Joseph II, who eased restrictions on Jews in the 1780s. Most of the old ghetto was cleared around 1900, but six synagogues, the Jewish Town Hall and the cemetery survived.

    Look for

    On the Jewish Town Hall, the lower clock has Hebrew numbers and its hands turn backwards, as Hebrew reads right to left.

  5. 05
    Culture · 1883

    National Theatre

    Built with money collected across the country, it burned in 1881 just before full opening and was rebuilt in two years. The words Národ sobě, the nation to itself, are written above the stage.

    Look for

    Above the front, bronze goddesses drive chariots pulled by three horses.

  6. 06
    Landmark

    Old Jewish Cemetery

    Burials took place here from the 15th century until 1787, with graves layered because space was short. Rabbi Judah Loew ben Bezalel, linked to the Golem legend, is buried here.

    Look for

    Carvings on the stones tell you about the dead: blessing hands for the Cohen families, a jug for the Levites, animals for family names.

  7. 07
    Square

    Old Town Square

    A marketplace since the 12th century, it was where 27 leaders of the Bohemian revolt were executed in 1621. Crosses set in the paving by the town hall mark the spot.

    Look for

    The Jan Hus monument in the centre was unveiled in 1915, five hundred years after the reformer was burned at the stake.

  8. 08
    Building

    Old-New Synagogue

    Built around 1270, it is the oldest active synagogue in Europe. Legend says the Golem made by Rabbi Löw still lies in its attic.

    Look for

    High on the outside wall, iron rungs climb to the attic door.

  9. 09
    Landmark · 1410

    Prague Astronomical Clock

    It was installed in 1410 by the clockmaker Mikuláš of Kadaň and is the oldest astronomical clock still working. The calendar dial below was painted by Josef Mánes in the 1860s.

    Look for

    Beside the upper dial, Death rings a bell and turns an hourglass, and the Turk beside him shakes his head.

  10. 10
    Palace

    Prague Castle

    Founded in the 9th century, it has been the seat of Bohemian kings, Holy Roman emperors and now the Czech president. The guard changes at the main gate every hour.

    Look for

    At the main gate, two stone giants club and stab their enemies above the guards’ heads.

  11. 11
    Church · 1929

    St. Vitus Cathedral

    Charles IV began it in 1344 with Matthias of Arras, and Peter Parler continued the work. It was finished only in 1929; the chapel of St Wenceslas guards the door to the crown jewels.

    Look for

    In a chapel on the left side of the nave, the stained-glass window was designed by Alfons Mucha.

  12. 12
    Square · 1348

    Wenceslas Square

    It began as a horse market in the New Town founded by Charles IV in 1348. Huge crowds gathered here in November 1989, during the days of the Velvet Revolution.

    Look for

    At the top, Josef Myslbek’s bronze St Wenceslas rides among four Czech patron saints. Praguers meet “under the horse”.
